correct.D: A SHA digest identifies one exact, immutable image manifest, so the deployment always runs the same build even if tags move.

incorrect.A: Tags are mutable: someone can re-push a different image under the same 'production' tag.
incorrect.B: Nightly rebuilds produce new images, which makes the running build less predictable, not more.
incorrect.C: 'latest' is the most mutable tag of all and changes on every push.

correct.D: Pod events and container logs show why the probe fails (wrong path, slow startup, app error), so they are the first thing to check.

incorrect.A: More replicas would just multiply restarting pods; the cause is not capacity.
incorrect.B: Lowering initialDelaySeconds makes probes start earlier and usually causes more failures. Change probe settings only after diagnosing.
incorrect.C: Node CPU and memory are normal, so the node is not the problem; draining it is disruptive and unlikely to help.

correct.B: Scale-to-zero requires the rule to allow all replicas to terminate (minimum replicas = 0), so no compute runs when the queue is empty.
correct.C: A KEDA-based scale rule that watches the Service Bus queue length starts replicas only when messages arrive.

incorrect.A: Raising the maximum replica count only sets an upper limit; it does nothing to reach zero when idle.
incorrect.D: HTTP concurrency scaling reacts to web requests, not to queue messages.

correct.A: A timer trigger gives the required regular scheduled rebuilds.
correct.B: A source code commit trigger rebuilds when application code changes.
correct.D: A base image update trigger rebuilds when the underlying OS/base image is updated.

incorrect.C: Registry events are not one of the three requirements (app change, base image change, schedule).
incorrect.E: A webhook is an outbound notification, not a build trigger for ACR Tasks.

correct: Ingress must be enabled first so the app is reachable over HTTPS.
Add the DNS records (CNAME/TXT) at the domain provider so ownership can be proven.
Validate the custom domain name once the DNS records exist.
Add the custom domain name to the container app after it is validated.
Bind the certificate last, to enable HTTPS for the domain.

correct.D: Session affinity is an HTTP ingress feature, and it works in single revision mode where all traffic goes to one active revision.

incorrect.A: TCP ingress does not support session affinity (it is an HTTP-level feature).
incorrect.B: TCP ingress does not support session affinity.
incorrect.C: Session affinity is only supported in single revision mode, not with multiple active revisions.

correct: Multiple revision mode allows several revisions to be active at once, so a new one can be tested without touching production traffic.
Traffic splitting assigns a percentage (here 20%) of requests to a specific revision.
incorrect: Single revision mode keeps only one active revision, so you cannot run a second one side by side.
Traffic isolation is not the feature used to route a percentage of requests.

correct: FROM sets the base image and must come first.
WORKDIR sets the working folder inside the image.
COPY brings the app files and setup script into the image.
RUN executes setupScript.ps1 at build time.
CMD defines what runs when the container starts (ContosoApp.dll).
A unique tag makes each image version identifiable.
Authenticating with Microsoft Entra ID is the secure way to push to ACR.
Pushing the image stores it in the registry for deployment.
incorrect: 'Build the image locally' is a step in the process but does not satisfy any of the three listed requirements.

correct: A HorizontalPodAutoscaler adds pods when CPU use is high (scale out).
A ClusterIP service exposes the app only inside the cluster.
incorrect: VerticalPodAutoscaler resizes the pod's CPU/memory; it does not add pods.
Ingress exposes services to outside traffic, the opposite of internal-only.
A Deployment runs the pods but does not autoscale or expose them.

correct.C: Multiple revision mode lets the old and new revisions run at the same time, which is needed to shift traffic gradually.
correct.E: Traffic splitting sets the percentage per revision, so you can shift gradually and roll back by moving traffic back.

incorrect.A: Single revision mode sends all traffic to one revision, so there is no gradual shift.
incorrect.B: Restarting a revision does not control traffic.
incorrect.D: More replicas add capacity but do not split traffic between revisions.

correct: Key Vault stores secrets (here a secret value) outside the app environment, and Container Apps references it.
A managed identity lets App1 authenticate to Key Vault without stored credentials.
incorrect: A Key Vault key is for cryptographic operations, not for storing a secret value.
A Container Apps secret lives inside the environment, which the requirement forbids.
Service principal and workload identity involve managing credentials or federation; managed identity is the simplest, credential-free option.

correct.A: A webhook can trigger an ACR build automatically on events, so builds run natively and automatically.
correct.D: A source-triggered task automatically builds when code is committed.

incorrect.B: A quick task is a one-off, manually started build, not automatic.
incorrect.C: Artifact cache rules cache images from upstream registries; they do not manage builds.

correct: Update the image tag in the deployment manifest to describe the new version.
Apply the updated manifest so Kubernetes performs a rolling update.
Verify the rollout status to confirm the update completed.
incorrect: Deleting and recreating the deployment causes downtime; it is not a rolling update.
Scaling to zero before updating also causes downtime.

correct: The managed identity must exist first.
Grant it the Key Vault Secrets User role so it can read secrets.
Then the app can retrieve the secret by using the SDK.
incorrect: An access policy with only the 'recover' permission is for restoring deleted secrets and does not allow reading them.
15.note: The source PDF shows these steps in a different order (grant, retrieve, assign). That order cannot work, so this site uses assign, grant, retrieve.

correct: More vCores raise compute throughput for similarity calculations, helping latency.
More memory keeps high-dimensional pgvector indexes resident in RAM.
Storage autoscale absorbs continuous growth from new embeddings.
incorrect: max_connections helps concurrency, not query speed or index residency.
Read replicas, backup retention and extra vCores do not address index residency or ingestion growth.

correct: The Azure Service Bus scaler triggers scaling from queue depth.
Minimum replicas = 0 allows scale-to-zero when the queue is empty.
Maximum replicas = 10 caps burst scaling.
incorrect: CPU and HTTP concurrency scalers react to CPU or web traffic, not queue depth.
Minimum replicas = 1 always keeps an instance running.
Letting the system choose the maximum replicas allows uncontrolled scaling.

correct: 'az containerapp env' manages the Container Apps environment, which is what shares the VNet, Dapr and logging settings.
'create' creates that environment.
--enable-workload-profiles lets you configure CPU and memory for containers.
incorrect: 'add-on' is not the right subcommand for creating an environment.
--enable-mtls and --internal-only do not provide configurable compute/memory profiles.

correct: App1 (Windows, deployed as code) must run for up to 10 minutes with event-driven scaling and the highest scale limit, which points to Premium.
App2 (Linux container) has the same needs, so Premium again.
incorrect: Consumption has a shorter maximum run time, and a lower scale limit than Premium.
Dedicated (App Service) plans scale on rules rather than events.

correct: 'az containerapp job' is the command group for scheduled and batch tasks.
'create' creates the job.
--trigger-type Schedule with the cron expression runs it every Sunday at midnight.
incorrect: 'env' manages environments, not jobs.
Event and Manual triggers do not run on a cron schedule.

correct: Build and push APP1 to ACR01 first.
Create an ACR task that tracks the base image for automatic rebuilds.
Grant the identity a role so the task can pull from the other registry.
Add credentials so the task can authenticate to the base-image registry.
Run the task to start the automated process.
'az containerapp' is the command group for container apps.
'ingress traffic set' assigns revision weights (80/20) to route traffic.
incorrect: 'container', 'network' and 'resource' are not Container Apps command groups.
'app', 'connection' and 'revision' do not set ingress traffic weights.

correct: Register the provider so the subscription can use Container Apps.
Create the Container Apps environment that the job runs in.
Create the job (with a schedule) to run the task at regular intervals.
incorrect: 'connected-env create' is for Azure Arc-enabled clusters.
'registry set' only matters for a private registry, which the question does not mention.
'job start' runs a job once manually; a scheduled job starts itself.
23.note: The source PDF lists registry set, connected-env create, job create. That differs from this answer, which follows the standard workflow.

correct: 'az acr' is the command group for registry tasks.
The trailing source location is the build context (the GitHub repo URL and branch).
incorrect: 'image' and 'automation' are not valid command groups for 'task create'.
'--arg' passes build arguments and '--target' selects a Dockerfile stage; neither supplies the source repository.

correct: Create the table with vector and metadata columns first.
Create the HNSW index for fast approximate similarity search.
Load the data (embeddings and metadata).
Query by using the <=> distance operator with a WHERE clause for metadata filtering.
incorrect: Increasing Redis memory is a caching task, not part of the retrieval workflow.
A B-tree index does not support vector similarity search.

correct.A: The case requires similarity calculations only against rows that satisfy metadata constraints, so index the metadata filter columns with a B-tree.

incorrect.B: max_connections affects concurrency, not query performance.
incorrect.C: shared_buffers helps caching generally but does not optimize filtered vector search.
incorrect.D: An IVFFlat index speeds the vector search but does not address the metadata-filter requirement.

correct: Managed identity meets the 'no plain-text credentials' policy.
A connection pooling library reuses connections for high concurrency and low latency.
A maximum pool size protects the database during spikes.
incorrect: Environment-variable credentials break the authentication policy.
An unlimited pool or higher max_connections can overwhelm the database.
Async execution and retry/backoff do not directly cap connections.

correct.A: Connection pooling reuses connections so many concurrent requests can be served efficiently.

incorrect.B: shared_buffers tunes memory caching, not connection handling.
incorrect.C: Read replicas scale reads but do not reduce connection overhead for the API.
incorrect.D: Raising max_connections allows more connections but increases memory pressure, without reuse.

correct: A time-to-live on each key makes entries expire automatically (10 minutes).
Publishing invalidation events lets the cache react to catalog updates.
Cache-aside with lazy loading serves repeated requests from the cache for low latency.
incorrect: RDB persistence is about durability, not expiration, freshness or latency.

correct.C: The lease container stores partition ownership, which lets multiple processor instances share the change feed load.

incorrect.A: Indexing precision affects vector index accuracy, not load balancing.
incorrect.B: Strong consistency is a consistency choice and does not distribute work.
incorrect.D: Autoscale throughput changes RU/s, not how work is split across instances.
